 JUDGMENT
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed by the petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. It is the specific case of the petitioner that on 23-09-2023 at about 3.00 a.m., while he was guiding a lorry bearing No.KA-03-AK-1373 to proceed towards Truck Bay line at FTI circle, Outer Ring road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru.

At that time, the driver of another lorry bearing No.KA-01-AM-5346 (hereinafter called as the offending lorry) drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to the said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and underwent surgery.
3. The petitioner contends that he has incurred expenses of approximately Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical treatment, food, nourishment, conveyance, and other incidental charges.
It is further stated that at the time of the accident, he was aged about 40 years and working as a Heavy Goods Vehicle (HGV) driver, earning Rs.40,000/- per month plus BATA of Rs.500/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, he claims to have suffered permanent disability resulting in loss of earning capacity and future income.
4. The petitioner asserts that the accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
Hence, he has sought compensation from Respondent No.1 and Respondent No.2, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle respectively.
5. Respondent No.1 (Owner) appeared through counsel and filed objections denying the entire averments made in the claim petition.
It is specifically contended that the alleged accident did not occur due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
On the contrary, it is asserted that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.

6. It is further contended that the driver of the offending lorry was holding a valid and effective driving licence and that the vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy as on the date of the accident.
On these grounds, Respondent No.1 has sought dismissal of the petition.
7. Respondent No.2 (Insurance Company) has also filed its written statement denying all material averments of the petition.

It is contended that the owner of the offending vehicle and the police authorities failed to comply with the mandatory provisions under Section 134(c) and Section 158(6)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, thereby rendering the petition not maintainable.

8. Though admitting the issuance and validity of the insurance policy as on the date of the accident,
Respondent No.2 has contended that its liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of the policy.

It is further pleaded that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid and Shakeel Ahmed vs Ayjaz Pasha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195862963/
2 effective driving licence at the time of the accident, and therefore the insurer is not liable to indemnify the insured.
9.

The insurer has also denied the allegations of negligence attributed to the driver of the offending lorry and has instead contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and the driver of lorry bearing registration No. KA-03- AK-1373, who allegedly reversed the vehicle without observing vehicular movement and dashed against the offending vehicle.

10. The insurance company has further denied the nature of injuries, age, avocation, income,
medical expenses, disability, and quantum of compensation claimed, terming the same as false,
exaggerated, and excessive.

11. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 23-09-2023 at about 3-00 a.m., FTI circle,
Outer Ring road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, he sustained injuries in a road traffic accident, while he was guiding the lorry bearing No.KA-01-AK-1373 to proceed towards truck bay line, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the lorry bearing No.KA-01-AM-5346?
2. Whether the Respondent No.2 proves that, the policy conditions are violated by Respondent No.1 and the Respondent No.2 is not liable to pay any compensation?
3. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation if any, how much, from whom?
4. What order or award ?
12.

In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.21.

On the other hand,
the Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW1.
13.

By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : In the negative.
Issue No.3: Partly in the affirmative.

Issue No.4: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 14.
ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 23-09-2023 at about 3.00 a.m., while he was guiding a lorry bearing No.KA-03-AK-1373 to proceed towards Truck Bay line at FTI circle, Outer Ring road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru.
At that time, the driver of the offending lorry drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.

Due to the said impact,
the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Shakeel Ahmed vs Ayjaz Pasha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195862963/
3 15.

In order to substantiate his case, the petitioner examined himself as PW1 and produced documentary evidence marked at Ex.P1 to Ex.P9, namely FIR, Complaint, Crime Detail Form, Spot Sketch, Notice, Reply Notice, IMV Report, Wound Certificate and Charge Sheet.
16. A careful perusal of Ex.P8 - Wound Certificate discloses that the petitioner sustained a crush injury of the left foot with rupture of underlying tendons.
The doctor has opined that the said injury is grievous in nature.

17. Further, after due investigation, the jurisdictional police have filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry, categorically alleging that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending driver.
The charge sheet prima facie establishes the culpability of the driver of the offending lorry.

18. Per contra, Respondent Nos.1 and 2 have contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner himself and the driver of the lorry bearing registration No.
KA-03-AK-1373 and not due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
In order to substantiate the said defence, an official of Respondent No.2 was examined as RW1, who reiterated the contents of the written statement.

19. During the cross-examination of PW1, the learned counsel for Respondent No.2 suggested that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of lorry bearing No. KA-03-AK-1373 and that if proper precautionary measures had been taken, the accident could have been avoided.
PW1 has categorically denied the said suggestion.

20. Except making bald suggestions in the cross- examination and taking up a plea in the written statement, the respondents have not produced any documentary evidence nor examined any independent witness to substantiate their contention of negligence of the petitioner.

21. On careful appreciation of the entire material on record, it is noticed that the FIR, Complaint,
Spot Sketch, IMV Report and Charge Sheet clearly indicate that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
The charge sheet filed by the jurisdictional police has not been challenged before any competent authority.

Except bare denial, no rebuttal evidence is placed on record to discredit the police investigation.
22.
It is a well-settled principle that proceedings under the Motor Vehicles Act are beneficial and summary in nature, and strict proof of negligence as required in a criminal trial is not necessary.

When the police investigation culminates in filing of a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and the same remains unchallenged, it carries prima facie evidentiary value.
23.
The oral testimony of PW1 is consistent and is duly corroborated by the contemporaneous police records and medical evidence.
There is no material contradiction elicited in his cross-examination so as to disbelieve his version.

Shakeel Ahmed vs Ayjaz Pasha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195862963/
4 24.

Therefore, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the petitioner has successfully proved that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
25. ISSUE NO.2:-
The respondent No.2 has contended that the owner of the offending vehicle violated the terms and condition incorporated in the policy.

However, on reading of entire material,
there is no evidence placed before the court to substantiate that the respondent no 1 committed any such violation.
It is evident that the offending vehicle was covered under a valid insurance policy at time of the accident.
Wherefore, the liability to compensate the petitioner rest with the respondent No.2.
Hence I answer this issue in the negative.
26. ISSUE NO.3:- Ex.P8 - Wound Certificate discloses that the petitioner sustained a grievous injury, namely crush injury of the left foot with rupture of underlying tendons.
The petitioner was immediately shifted to Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bengaluru, where he took treatment as an inpatient for seven days.

Thereafter, he was admitted to Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics,
Bengaluru, and treated as an inpatient for 18 days.

sentences.text: 27. The petitioner contends that he has incurred an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical expenses, medicines, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
It is further stated that at the time of the accident, he was aged about 41 years and was working as a Heavy Goods Vehicle driver earning Rs.40,000/- per month plus BATA of Rs.500/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, he claims loss of earning capacity and future income.

28. In order to prove the disability, the petitioner examined Dr. Chidananda K.G., Orthopaedic Surgeon at Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma and Orthopaedics, as PW2, and produced documents at Ex.P19 to Ex.

sentences.text: PW2 deposed that the petitioner had sustained post-traumatic injury to the left foot and was initially treated at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital.
He underwent surgery in the form of wound debridement and VAC dressing, and subsequently split skin grafting (SSG) was performed at their hospital.

PW2 further stated that at present the petitioner complains of restricted range of movement of the ankle and sub- talar joint, pain during movement, difficulty in crossing legs, sitting, squatting and using Indian toilet, and difficulty in performing certain daily activities.
30. PW2 assessed the permanent physical disability at 40% to the left lower limb and 13.33% to the whole body.
However, in the cross-examination, PW2 admitted that he had not personally treated the petitioner and that the fractures had united.

31. It is pertinent to note that the injury sustained is to the left foot, which plays a significant role in mobility, balance and performance of routine as well as occupational activities, particularly in the case of a Heavy Goods Vehicle driver.
Any impairment in this region would undoubtedly cause difficulty in prolonged driving and operating heavy vehicles.

Shakeel Ahmed vs Ayjaz Pasha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195862963/
5 32.

However, though PW2 has assessed physical disability, he has not specifically opined regarding functional disability, i.e., the actual impact of the injury on the earning capacity of the petitioner,
considering his avocation, age and nature of work.

33. Having regard to: the nature and location of the injury, the fact that fractures have united, the occupation of the petitioner as a driver and the overall evidence on record, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the functional disability affecting the earning capacity of the petitioner can be reasonably assessed at 7% to the whole body for the purpose of calculating future loss of income and awarding just compensation.
34. On perusal of the petition and the documents produced, it is seen that the petitioner has mentioned his age as 40 years.
However, Ex. P-10, the driving licence, shows his date of birth as 14-02-1982.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident, the petitioner was 41 years of age.

Accordingly, the proper multiplier applicable to this case is 14, as per the settled principles laid down in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation [(2009) 6 SCC 121.
35.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioner has asserted that he was a HGV driver, earning a sum of Rs.40,000/- per month + Batta of Rs.500/- per day.
Due to the accidental injuries he has suffered loss of earning capacity and future income.
36. The petitioner has not produced any documents to substantiate his avocation and income.
In the absence of material evidence relating to the source of income, the tribunal is required to consider the notional income as per the guidelines of the Lok Adalath.
The accident is stated to have occurred in the year 2023.

Therefore, income of the petitioner is assessed at 16,000/- P.M.
37.

Accordingly, this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner, having sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
38.

Loss of future income on account of permanent disability: Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 7% is reasonable and just.
39. The petitioner was 41 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 14.
The notional income taken as Rs.16,000 x 12 x 14 x 7/100= Rs.1,88,160/- towards loss of future income.
40. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .50,000/- would be just and fair compensation under the head of Pain and sufferings Shakeel Ahmed vs Ayjaz Pasha on 5 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195862963/
6
41 . Loss of amenities of life:
undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .30,000/- under the head of loss of amenities of life.
42. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.12 amounting to Rs.2,40,710/-.
There is no evidence forthcoming to disbelieve the said medical bills.
On perusal of medical bills, it appears that the petitioner has spent Rs.2,40,710/- towards medical treatment.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded compensation of .2,40,710/- towards Medical Expenses.
43. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:

Ex.P.11 -Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was admitted at Kanva Sri Sai Hospital, Bengaluru, as an inpatient from 23-9-2023 to 26-09-2023 and again from 10-10-2023 to 12-10- 2023 and at Sanjaygandhi hospital, Bengaluru from 30-10-2023 to 16-11-2023 i.e., totally for a period of 25 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .25,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
44. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery,
this tribunal considers the 4 months for rest is considered .
As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 4 = Rs.64,000/-. loss of earning during laid up period.

45. Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:
 Sl. Nature of Compensation Amount  No.
 1. Loss of future earnings . 1,88,160/-
 2. Pain and Sufferings . 50,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities . 30,000/-
 4. Medical expenses  2,40,710/-
 5. Conveyance, Food, . 25,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  charges  6. Loss of income during . 64,000/-
 laid up period  Total . 5,97,870/-
46.
Liability:
Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.

7 47.
ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above Issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,97,870/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 2 years and balance 75% shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

 1. Loss of future earnings . 1,88,160/-
 2. Pain and Sufferings . 50,000/-
 3. Loss of amenities . 30,000/-
 4. Medical expenses  2,40,710/-
 5. Conveyance, Food, . 25,000/-
 Nourishment & Attendant  charges  6. Loss of income during . 64,000/-
 laid up period  Total . 5,97,870/-
46.
Respondent No.1 being the owner and the Respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner with interest at 6% p.a.
With these observation I answer Issue No.3 partly in the affirmative.

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to above Issues,
I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.5,97,870/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.2 shall pay the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount 25% of the amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank of his choice for a period of 2 years and balance 75% shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
